analysis.title: The Hedge That Stopped Hedging: AI Default Swaps Hit Records As Goldman Finds Credit Cracking Everywhere Except The Index
key_insights: Five-year CDS on Intel, Amazon, Broadcom, Microsoft, Alphabet and SpaceX hit record highs on Friday (Oct 30) after Intel's weak guidance and Amazon's cash burn, per ICE data cited by Bloomberg. Intel's 5Y CDS rose as much as 22.4bps in one morning to 127.9bps.

CDX IG finished the week 1.5bps tighter at 62bps while single-name AI CDS widened. The average AI name in CDX IG went from about 67bps to about 140bps over six months, and the index drifted from the mid-50s to around 60bps.

Bloomberg reports CDX has widened at less than a fifth of the pace of the US high-grade bond index. The correlation between the two has fallen to about half its five-year average. On Friday hyperscaler CDS widened 3bps to 9.8bps while CDX IG rose by less than 1bp.

Goldman's Pasi says vol, tranche and curve markets never fully confirmed the rally in spot synthetics, which suggests investors are reluctant to abandon hedges. Cash IG spreads widened to 90bps, the widest since late March, and HY OAS reached 340bps, the widest since May 2025.

Goldman's Lynam recommends keeping macro index hedges, arguing that once AI risk threatens the supply of capital for the buildout, the impact spreads across credit. 3-month implied vol is close to post-COVID medians in USD credit and at the 65th percentile in EUR credit, and skew has flattened, which improves the payoff on outright payers.

Goldman's credit portfolio trading desk (LaCaze) favors shorting a basket of 30-year IG bonds excluding hyperscalers (~107bps, 115 CUSIPs) against Treasuries on swap. The basket costs about 16.9bps a year in negative carry. Generic ex-hyperscaler IG spread sits at the 12th percentile on a 20-year lookback.
Goldman's Biswas will not spend theta on a moderate-widening hedge. He expects a further risk-off leg to send spreads into tail zones rather than settle 10bps wider in IG or 50bps wider in HY.

Supply is the driver. IG issuance was $60B across 23 deals last week versus $30-35B expected, led by Microsoft's $25B deal (its first outright bond since 2017, $115B of orders). YTD IG issuance passed $2T, beating 2020's full-year record, and global hyperscaler issuance is $254B, above GIR's $250B year-end forecast.

Goldman's 30-year hyperscaler basket had its most volatile week of the year, averaging 6.3bps a day. It rallied 17bps on Meta's $95B equity financing plan and Oracle's investor day, then gave it back on weak core-business earnings, Meta turning FCF-negative and the Microsoft deal. The IG desk's bias is to sell rallies, with spreads near YTD wides possibly offering tactical opportunities for selective length.

HY ended the week 3bps wider but with a violent round trip. HY OAS went from 337bps to 312bps by Wednesday, then to 340bps by Friday. The CCC index tightened 30bps on Tuesday to 1,088bps, then gave back 28bps by Friday.

HY AI spreads widened to 389bps versus 263bps for non-AI BB/Bs. 25 HY index bonds fell 5+ points on the week, 12 of them CCC or worse. 5.31% of the CCC-or-lower bucket fell 5+ points versus a 1.2% median week, and the metric has been above 5% for four weeks. The 6-week count of 5+ point decliners is 147.
Goldman's GIR team is neutral on HY AI credit (especially project finance), underweight CCCs, and prefers single-Bs over BBs because it expects BBs to absorb future AI-related financing.

Leveraged loans are up 3.04% YTD versus +0.60% for HY and -1.17% for IG, but 53 loans moved more than 3 points last week and loan funds had their first weekly outflow since the week ended June 24. 53% of distressed loans mature within three years, and software is 32% of distressed volume versus a 12% index weight.
Fitch's default rate across about 1,500 US private debt borrowers set another quarterly record at 6.3%.

The 20 largest actively managed IG and HY funds trailed benchmarks by about 0.7% (IG) and 0.6% (HY) over the past month. Goldman's portfolio trading channel had $33.2B of inquiry across 433 inquiries, with IG clients net sellers 1.3:1 by DV01 and CCC holders selling 1.7:1.

Biswas is worried about France. The 10Y OAT-Bund spread last traded above 150bps in 2012, when debt-to-GDP was below 90%. It is now above 120% and the economy shrank in Q3. French financials CDS widened 27.6bps in two months versus 11.6bps for non-French financials, while European AT1s trade near decade tights.

Goldman strategists give a qualified yes on credit. The macro baseline is good enough for higher-quality credit, but the left tail of growth is thicker and they do not view broad-based dip buying as prudent. Week-ahead catalysts include midterms Tuesday, the Treasury refunding Wednesday, Apple and Palantir earnings, a BoE decision and October payrolls Friday.

sector_views.rationale: Macro baseline is good enough for higher-quality credit, but heavy hyperscaler supply and a thicker left tail argue against broad dip buying. The IG desk's bias is to sell rallies.
GIR is neutral on HY AI credit and underweight CCCs. 5+ point decliners are running at more than four times the normal rate, and security selection matters more than CCC beta.
Software is 32% of distressed loan volume versus a 12% index weight, and AI is eroding its borrowers.

earnings_insights: Intel guided sharply lower last week (guidance figures not given in the note), pushing its 5Y CDS to a record 127.9bps.
Meta's CDS hit a record after its Oct 22 quarter, and Meta turned FCF-negative. The note says hyperscalers burned $31B in Q3.
Goldman says Microsoft is now the only major hyperscaler generating positive FCF.
Apple and Palantir report earnings in the week ahead (week of Nov 2).

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Lynam says index hedges are not expensive. 3-month implied vol is near post-COVID medians in USD and skew has flattened. Macro hedges stay useful because AI stress becomes a broad growth and capital-supply problem.
tension_points.bear_case: Single-name AI CDS sit at records while CDX IG is tighter, and the correlation between CDX and the IG bond index has fallen to about half its five-year average. Commerzbank's Stoeckle says index overlay demand might not rise much if single names are the hedge of choice.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler financing conditions deteriorating enough to leak into broad IG cash, which the PT desk says would make ex-hyperscaler names catch up on widening.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman strategists see the macro baseline as good enough for higher-quality credit, and technical demand has so far offset supply.
tension_points.bear_case: The left tail of the growth distribution is thicker, IG supply passed $2T, and AI issuance is testing investor appetite. Biswas expects spreads to air-pocket into tail zones in a further risk-off leg.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Technical demand failing to absorb continued hyperscaler supply without greater spread concessions.

tension_points.bull_case: Only $2.04B of new loans launched last week, CLO demand keeps absorbing paper, CLO AAAs are 3-4bps off tights, and only 7.4% of the market trades at par or above.
tension_points.bear_case: 53% of distressed loans mature within three years, refi exits for CCC issuers are narrow, and software is 32% of distressed volume.
